Zbarazh Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Zbarazh's Jewish community, present from the late 15th century, survived the Khmelnytsky massacres of 1648–49, Turkish occupation in 1675, and Haidamak raids in 1798. From 1858 to 1893, Ishiyagu Babad served as head of the town's religious court, and Zbarazh became one of the earliest centers of the Haskalah (Jewish Enlightenment) in Galicia; a Hasidic court founded by Yom Tov-Lipman Geller was also seated here in the early 20th century. The population peaked at 3,768 (46.7 percent of the town) in 1880. Following the German occupation of July 1941, 76 Jews — mostly intellectuals — were executed in the Lubianki forest that September; the ghetto's eventual liquidation on June 8, 1943, followed mass deportations to the Bełżec extermination camp. This is the older of Zbarazh's two Jewish cemeteries, vandalized during WWII.
